title: BGM gets corrupted, is there a reason?

posts.author: isaac3000
posts.body:
Hello everyone.
I am using the RPG Maker Sound Color files available for free from Aaron Krogh. They are fantastic and I really want to keep using them.
The files are fine (except for a couple that never play for me), when I want to listen to them outside the engine, they are sounding great.
When I add them to my game, they also work fine until randomly they don't anymore. When they start playing in a cutscene they make a weird start/stop noise, like it's buffering or something.
So I have to go to Resource Manager (F10), delete the bgm, import it again from the folder and then it is working for some time.
After a while, it gets corrupted again. I noticed this only with these files. So, is there a way to prevent this from happening?
Thanks in advance!

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
If the files really get corrupted, you have a much bigger problem. You might have a virus, or your hard disk is getting old. A virus is curable, but dying of age is something no-one can escape.
I'd run some scans if I were you. And if everything is clean, make up backups (and save them on any medium you like, other than your current computer) for all your important stuff before it's too late.
I don't see how a file can work fine, and than just start acting up, just by it being played by your game. That doesn't happen, because your game doesn't overwrite those files. So if it is not a virus, and not your hard disk, than... idk...
---
However... What if the files are not corrupted at all? You say it sounds like buffering... How large are your files? Maybe it IS buffering.
If your files are very large, you can pre-load them. Simply play the file at the start of the scene, at volume 0. It can be overwritten by another command straight away, if you want other music to play untill this music is called, as long as you call for it a few seconds or more before you need it.
Do this for all the files you want to use in that scene, just on the top of the event is fine.
Now all the files are loaded before they are played, eliminating all the loading lag.

Well, that depends on the computer you use. If you work on a pentium 4, you will experience more issues than on a i7. Your graphics card is important too.
I can tell from experience that RPG maker VX Ace can dealbwith older computers really well, but on older computers, things like file size and such become more important.
Don't scan your disk on viruses alone. If the files are corrupt, it's way more likely your hard disk is dying. The never your disk is, the more likely it is.
-----
Another possibility...
Do you use A cloud storage service? Like dropbox, onedrive or google drive? Or maybe a private server? And do you load, test and edit directly on the server?
If the answer is yes, we found your problem. Work on a local copy of your game. Cloud servers are perfect for back up, not so much for work space.
If you happen to have an app installed, and you want to keep working in the onedrive or Dropbox folder, turn off auto-sync.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Really? That was such a shot in the dark. I didn't really think
The fact that it has to read the music from a server while playing, is enough to cause lag at least. This is probably the problem. So, to be clear, I still think your files are NOT corrupt.
I didn't mean to give you a scare. Earlier I said that if the files were corrupt, it might be HDD failure, but I thought the problem was probably not corrupt file, but file size, or something.
Turns out it is probably the cloud service. Once copied over to your harddisk, everything probably runs just fine and no files are corrupt.
However, if it turns out your files are corrupt and it happened on the server, it can be a few things:
- Terrible connection while uploading
- Terrible cloud service
Again, cloud service is perfect for backups, not for workspace.
Let me know if this fixes it.
(Edit: When I say "old", I mean 7 or 8 years, or even older. And mostly about desktops. This isn't really a thing in modern laptops with an SSD.)
